title: Quantile monitoring pipeline and slice-based regression detector for route/model/region
creator: Maya Gupta
description:
Goal: Build a production-ready quantile monitoring pipeline that computes p50/p95/p99 per route, per model, and per region; expose 1m/5m/1h rollups; and add a slice-based regression detector with automatic alerting and dashboard views. Success metrics: p95/p99 rollups available for 95% of traffic slices, regression false positive rate < 5% after one tuning cycle, and alert mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) < 15 minutes for P0 regressions.

Scope and deliverables:
- Ingest raw request traces (latency, model, route, region, token count) from tracing pipeline into a streaming aggregator.
- Produce continuous quantile rollups at 1-minute, 5-minute, and 1-hour granularity keyed by route/model/region and by sequence-length bucket.
- Backfill job to compute historical quantiles from raw traces for the last 90 days.
- Implement regression detector that compares current-window p95/p99 to adaptive baseline using EWMA and percentile-delta thresholds with noise-aware smoothing.
- Dashboard set: (1) Traffic-normalized percentile tiles per route/model/region, (2) Quantile drift swimlane for top 50 routes, (3) Tokens/sec heatmap across regions, (4) Slice explorer to pivot by model, region, route, and sequence-length.
- Alerting: PagerDuty + Slack with runbook links and automatic attribution hints (e.g., model variant change, region degradation).
- UX: per-route historical quantile overlay + annotation of deploys and config changes.

Non-goals: full A/B automatic rollback, full integration with customer-facing incident flows (follow-up ticket), or sampling changes to upstream traces (we will work with Observability team).
acceptance_criteria: Streaming rollups emit p50/p95/p99 for route/model/region at 1m/5m/1h
Backfill completes for last 90 days and matches streaming rollups within 1% for high-traffic slices
Regression detector generates alerts with simulated injected regressions in the load harness and meets <5% false positive rate after tuning
Dashboard templates live in Console with filterable pivots and exportable CSV for selected slices
Runbook and PagerDuty integration verified with a test alert and MTTA measured
comments: 2026-02-13 - Maya Gupta: Drafted initial design with Observability. Decided to use streaming rollups instead of naive full-aggregation for latency percentiles to control cost and latency of dashboards.
2026-02-18 - Omar Delgado: Implemented prototype aggregator using t-digest for approximate quantiles. Accuracy tests on p95 showed 0.7% median error for high-traffic slices.
2026-02-25 - Priya Nair (Reviews): Suggested adding sequence-length bucketing to account for workload variance; added to scope. Also asked for backfill for historical baselining.

2026-03-02 - Infrastructure feedback (Elliot Park): Need retention plan for raw traces to support 90-day backfill; opened infra ticket to extend trace retention for slices above threshold. Infra will provide ephemeral storage for backfill jobs.

2026-03-05 - Omar Delgado: Regression detector POC implemented. Using EWMA on p95 deltas with per-slice variance normalization. Ran load harness with synthetic 20% latency shift; detector fired and generated Slack/PagerDuty test notification.
2026-03-08 - UX review (Lina Morales): Dashboard prototypes reviewed; requested a compare-to-baseline toggle and deploy annotations. Also asked for exportable CSV for slices for offline analysis.
2026-03-10 - Maya Gupta: Merged initial PR for streaming rollups. Next steps: finish backfill job, wire up dashboard panels, and run two-week tuning window to calibrate thresholds.
notes: Design trade-offs: t-digest gives cost/latency benefits but has higher error on tiny slices; we'll fallback to exact histograms for slices above critical traffic thresholds.
Alert sensitivity plan: start with conservative thresholds to reduce noise, then ramp sensitivity after two-week operator tuning window. Documented in Confluence linked artifact.
Data cardinality control: we'll limit top-K models per route for fine-grained rollups and use 'other' bucket for long-tail to bound storage costs.
